day: # The Church in Wales' Sunday and holy-day Eucharist lectionary, kept as the
# with the rows below for what the Church in Wales reads differently.  From
# the Church in Wales, "Lectionary Year A, Weekdays 2, Advent 2025 ~ Kingdom
# 2026" (English), compiled by Ritchie Craven, Principal Service columns
# (read October 2026); its Year B successor, "Lectionary Year B, Weekdays 1
# Advent 2026 ~ Kingdom 2027", Advent to the First Sunday after Trinity
# (read October 2026, the rest not readable); and "Lectionary, Book Two: Holy
# Days and other services" for Peter (or Peter and Paul) and the Welsh
# (read October 2026, through a text extract: check against the PDF).
# The departures are those of the Church of England's Common Worship
# Principal Service lectionary (cofe-cw.csv), but the psalms are cited, as
# the booklet says, "as they appear in scripture" (the RCL's numbering).
#   Rows marked A or B are only those the two booklets show; Year C, and
#   Year B after the First Sunday after Trinity, are still the plain RCL.
#   Shorter psalm portions the booklet offers beside the RCL's ("Psalm 148
#   or 148. 7-14") and brackets on verses the RCL already reads are not given.
#   The Second Sunday before Lent (kept after 2 February) displaces the RCL

# Days"), with "The Supplementary Collects, Epistles, and Gospels" (pp.
# 309-321): "The following may be used on the appropriate commemorations ...
# provided that no special provision has been made for the day" (so not on
# a Sunday).  St Joseph, the Name of Jesus, the Beheading of St John the
# Baptist and Holy Cross Day have their own (the Epistle and Gospel of the
# day the book names); the days of the Blessed Virgin Mary hers; the others
# the common their entry in the Calendar describes (a woman: Of a Virgin or
# Matron; a martyr; a missionary; a doctor; a bishop; a poet, scholar or
# translator: Of a Doctor of the Church, Poet, or Scholar; any other: Of Any
# Saint, from the Octave of All Saints, p. 304), and the Canadian and
# historical entries the Founders, Benefactors and Missionaries (p. 302:
# "or on historical anniversaries").  The choice of common is the project's.
# Introit and psalm Between Lections from the table on p. liii and the
# commons' footnotes (Of Any Saint: the table's Ps. 92. 12-15, the footnote
# printing 97); the last verse of each lesson is the last the book prints.
